The new backup-code branch runs whenever `credentials.backupCode` is present. Therefore a request can authenticate to a password-protected account by sending a valid backup code plus an arbitrary non-empty `totpCode`, causing the password check to be skipped. The same logic also allows login with only a valid TOTP code and no password for password-based accounts. Second factors should be checked in addition to the password, not as a replacement for it; verify the password for accounts that have one regardless of whether a TOTP or backup code is supplied."

      "title": "Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write and can allow reuse",
      "body": "Backup-code login decrypts the stored array, finds the used index, sets that entry to null, then writes the whole array back. Two concurrent login requests using the same backup code can both read the array before either update is committed, causing both requests to succeed and defeating the one-time-use property. Use a database transaction with re-reading/locking, an atomic conditional update, or store backup codes as individually hashed/used records."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx",

      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "QR-screen Continue button submits the TOTP enable form",
      "body": "The Continue button on the QR-code step has `type=\"submit\"` and is inside the outer form whose submit handler calls `handleEnable`, but its `onClick` only changes the step and does not call `preventDefault`. Clicking it therefore sends an enable request with an empty TOTP code before/while navigating to the OTP step, causing spurious errors or race conditions. It should be `type=\"button\"` or prevent the default submit behavior."
    },

      "body": "After 2FA is enabled, the modal shows backup codes. Only the explicit Close button calls `resetState()` and `onEnable()`. The dialog still allows dismissal through `onOpenChange`, so if the user closes the modal by overlay/escape/close UI, the component can remain mounted with `step` still set to `DisplayBackupCodes` and the backup codes still in state. Reopening the modal may then show backup codes again without re-authentication, and the parent screen may not refresh to show that 2FA is enabled. The backup-code step should block dismissal or perform the same cleanup/notification on dismiss."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/components/auth/TwoFactor.tsx",

      "severity": "medium",

If a user enters a six-digit code and then clears the inputs, react-hook-form keeps the previous TOTP value, so a later submission or auto-submit may send a stale code. The effect should always synchronize the form value, including setting an empty string when the input value is empty."

Because backup-code login and disabling 2FA with a backup code are security-critical paths, they should have explicit automated coverage."
    },

      "file": "apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx",
      "line": 188,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Empty backup code can be submitted without a useful validation error",
      "body": "The login form uses `noValidate`, and the Zod schema only validates email/password while passing other fields through. The BackupCode input's native `required` attribute is therefore not enforced, so submitting an empty backup code sends an empty string. The server then responds as if a second factor is still required, and the UI does not show an incorrect-backup-code or required-field error. Add schema validation or explicit handling for an empty backup code."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts",
      "line": 61,
      "severity": "low",

      "title": "Disable endpoint assumes backupCode is a string and can throw a 500",
      "body": "`req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(\"-\", \"\")` will throw a TypeError if the request body supplies a non-string value such as an object, array, or number. This turns malformed input into an internal server error instead of a validation failure. Validate the request body shape and types before using string methods."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts",
      "line": 144,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Backup code comparison is case-sensitive while the UI suggests uppercase codes",
      "body": "Generated backup codes are lowercase hexadecimal strings, and the server only strips dashes before comparing. The login input placeholder uses `XXXXX-XXXXX`, which may lead users to enter uppercase letters. Since the comparison is case-sensitive, uppercase input will be rejected even if the code is otherwise correct. Normalize backup codes by trimming whitespace and lowercasing before comparison on the server, and ideally enforce the same on the client."

findings.title: Password verification is skipped when any totpCode is present, allowing backup-code login without a password
findings.body: In the credentials authorize function, the password is only verified when `user.password && !credentials.totpCode`. The new backup-code branch runs whenever `credentials.backupCode` is present. Therefore a request can authenticate to a password-protected account by sending a valid backup code plus an arbitrary non-empty `totpCode`, causing the password check to be skipped. The same logic also allows login with only a valid TOTP code and no password for password-based accounts. Second factors should be checked in addition to the password, not as a replacement for it; verify the password for accounts that have one regardless of whether a TOTP or backup code is supplied.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write and can allow reuse
findings.body: Backup-code login decrypts the stored array, finds the used index, sets that entry to null, then writes the whole array back. Two concurrent login requests using the same backup code can both read the array before either update is committed, causing both requests to succeed and defeating the one-time-use property. Use a database transaction with re-reading/locking, an atomic conditional update, or store backup codes as individually hashed/used records.

findings.title: QR-screen Continue button submits the TOTP enable form
findings.body: The Continue button on the QR-code step has `type="submit"` and is inside the outer form whose submit handler calls `handleEnable`, but its `onClick` only changes the step and does not call `preventDefault`. Clicking it therefore sends an enable request with an empty TOTP code before/while navigating to the OTP step, causing spurious errors or race conditions. It should be `type="button"` or prevent the default submit behavior.

findings.title: Backup-code screen can be dismissed without resetting state or notifying the parent
findings.body: After 2FA is enabled, the modal shows backup codes. Only the explicit Close button calls `resetState()` and `onEnable()`. The dialog still allows dismissal through `onOpenChange`, so if the user closes the modal by overlay/escape/close UI, the component can remain mounted with `step` still set to `DisplayBackupCodes` and the backup codes still in state. Reopening the modal may then show backup codes again without re-authentication, and the parent screen may not refresh to show that 2FA is enabled. The backup-code step should block dismissal or perform the same cleanup/notification on dismiss.

findings.title: TOTP form value is not cleared when the digit inputs are emptied
findings.body: The effect only calls `methods.setValue("totpCode", value)` when `value` is truthy. If a user enters a six-digit code and then clears the inputs, react-hook-form keeps the previous TOTP value, so a later submission or auto-submit may send a stale code. The effect should always synchronize the form value, including setting an empty string when the input value is empty.

findings.title: Assertion checks Promise truthiness instead of checkbox state
findings.body: `await expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts that the Promise returned by `isChecked()` is truthy, which is always true, so the test can pass even if the 2FA switch is not checked. Use `await expect(page.locator(...)).toBeChecked()` or await the boolean result explicitly.

findings.title: No e2e coverage for using backup codes to log in or disable 2FA
findings.body: The PR adds backup codes as an authentication fallback, but the tests only cover displaying/copying/downloading them and leave a TODO for login/disable flows. Because backup-code login and disabling 2FA with a backup code are security-critical paths, they should have explicit automated coverage.

findings.title: Empty backup code can be submitted without a useful validation error
findings.body: The login form uses `noValidate`, and the Zod schema only validates email/password while passing other fields through. The BackupCode input's native `required` attribute is therefore not enforced, so submitting an empty backup code sends an empty string. The server then responds as if a second factor is still required, and the UI does not show an incorrect-backup-code or required-field error. Add schema validation or explicit handling for an empty backup code.

findings.title: Disable endpoint assumes backupCode is a string and can throw a 500
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` will throw a TypeError if the request body supplies a non-string value such as an object, array, or number. This turns malformed input into an internal server error instead of a validation failure. Validate the request body shape and types before using string methods.

findings.title: Backup code comparison is case-sensitive while the UI suggests uppercase codes
findings.body: Generated backup codes are lowercase hexadecimal strings, and the server only strips dashes before comparing. The login input placeholder uses `XXXXX-XXXXX`, which may lead users to enter uppercase letters. Since the comparison is case-sensitive, uppercase input will be rejected even if the code is otherwise correct. Normalize backup codes by trimming whitespace and lowercasing before comparison on the server, and ideally enforce the same on the client.
